task_instance: Design a single, consolidated agent-facing tool (per the skill's own consolidation example: replacing separate list_users/list_events/create_event tools with one comprehensive tool) named `calendar_schedule_event`: write its tool description (what/when/inputs/returns), a full JSON Schema for its input with types/constraints/defaults/examples, a machine-readable success (concise+detailed) and error return shape with actionable recovery guidance, verb-noun namespaced naming, and a real working implementation backed by an in-memory calendar store. Then verify the design against the skill's Tool Audit Checklist by running the tool with valid calls, a real scheduling conflict, and malformed calls.
evidence: Wrote /tmp/.../tool_catalog.py containing: TOOL_NAME='calendar_schedule_event' (verb-noun, namespaced), TOOL_DESCRIPTION answering what/when(+when-not)/returns, INPUT_SCHEMA as a full JSON Schema (types, min/max, enum, defaults, format examples, additionalProperties:false), a ToolError class producing structured {error_code, message, invalid_value, expected_format, recovery, retryable} payloads, and a real calendar_schedule_event() implementation that validates input, searches an in-memory CalendarStore for the first mutually free 15-min-aligned slot, and books it. Wrote /tmp/.../test_tool_catalog.py which validates INPUT_SCHEMA is a legal JSON Schema (jsonschema.Draft7Validator.check_schema), confirms a well-formed call validates and a malformed attendee id is rejected by the schema itself, runs the tool against a store with a pre-seeded scheduling conflict for one attendee and confirms it correctly skips the conflicting 09:00-10:00 block and books 10:00-10:30 (proving the consolidated find-availability-and-book workflow works in one call), checks concise vs detailed response shapes, and triggers two error paths (INVALID_ATTENDEE_ID, INVALID_TIMESTAMP) confirming each carries a concrete invalid_value, expected_format, and recovery string per the skill's error-message-design and audit-checklist requirements. Ran `python3 test_tool_catalog.py` in the work directory: all 24 checks printed PASS, script exited 0 with final line 'All checks passed: tool contract satisfies the skill's audit checklist.' This is the core deliverable of the tool-design skill (a designed and verified tool contract), fully produced and verified without needing any external service, credential, or missing bundled script -- the skill's references/ directory (best_practices.md, architectural_reduction.md) is optional further reading, not a required input to the deliverable, and was confirmed absent (only LICENSE and SKILL.md exist next to the skill).
